title: 31yo F Amniotic Fluid Embolism
background: Para 2 at 39+4 weeks, in established labour, 8 cm dilated, on an oxytocin infusion for augmentation. Membranes ruptured artificially eleven minutes ago. She said she felt suddenly cold and frightened, then had a brief seizure and collapsed. This sense of impending doom immediately preceding collapse is described in a large proportion of cases and is often the only warning. The obstetric emergency call goes out at 03:14.

exam.finding: Unresponsive, cyanosed, gasping, in extremis within four minutes of feeling unwell. The speed of deterioration is itself diagnostic
Central cyanosis of the lips and tongue, frothy blood-stained secretions at the mouth, no facial or airway swelling and no urticaria, which argues against anaphylaxis

Tachycardia at 148/min, profound hypotension, impalpable radial pulses with a weak central pulse, capillary refill over 6 seconds. Initial right ventricular failure from acute pulmonary vasoconstriction, followed within minutes by left ventricular failure
Widespread coarse crackles, saturations 72% on 15 L/min, poor air entry, no wheeze, no unilateral absence of breath sounds

Gravid uterus, hypertonic and firm, fetal heart rate 68 bpm and falling on the cardiotocograph. Torrential fresh vaginal bleeding beginning about eight minutes after collapse as the coagulopathy establishes

Cyanosed and mottled, bleeding freely from the intravenous cannula site and from the epidural insertion site, no rash. Oozing from every puncture site is the visible marker of disseminated intravascular coagulation
GCS 6, post-ictal, pupils 4 mm and sluggish. Neurological injury here is hypoxic and is determined by how fast circulation is restored

investigations.name: Fibrinogen, INR and platelets
investigations.report: Fulminant disseminated intravascular coagulation. Fibrinogen collapsing from a pregnancy baseline of 4 to 6 g/L to under 0.5 within minutes is close to specific for amniotic fluid embolism among obstetric catastrophes.

investigations.name: Arterial blood gas
investigations.report: Profound mixed acidosis with severe hypoxaemia.

investigations.name: Bedside transthoracic echocardiogram
investigations.report: Severely dilated, poorly contracting right ventricle with septal bowing into the left ventricle and a small underfilled left ventricle. No pericardial effusion. This right ventricular failure pattern guides treatment: it demands vasopressor and pulmonary vasodilator support, and it means aggressive fluid loading will make things worse.

investigations.name: Haemoglobin (serial)
investigations.report: Rapid fall from postpartum haemorrhage on a background of complete coagulopathy.

investigations.name: 12-Lead ECG
investigations.report: Sinus tachycardia at 146/min with right axis deviation, S1Q3T3 pattern and T wave inversion in V1 to V4. Acute right heart strain. Indistinguishable from massive pulmonary thromboembolism on ECG alone.

investigations.name: Ionised calcium
investigations.report: Hypocalcaemia from massive transfusion with citrated products. Calcium is required for both coagulation and myocardial contractility and is repeatedly forgotten during massive transfusion.

data.label: Obstetric emergency call, left lateral displacement, airway and oxygen
actions: Activate obstetric and neonatal emergency teams

doseMap.Manual left uterine displacement: Rather than a tilted table, since effective chest compressions require a flat surface. Aortocaval compression by a term uterus can halve cardiac output during CPR

data.label: Prepare for perimortem caesarean section within 4 minutes if she arrests
actions: Assign a timekeeper who announces elapsed minutes aloud

doseMap.Scalpel at the bedside: If cardiac arrest occurs at over 20 weeks gestation, delivery must begin by 4 minutes and be completed by 5. This is done at the bedside, not in theatre, and it is done primarily to improve maternal resuscitation by relieving aortocaval compression

data.label: Support the right ventricle, do not flood it

doseMap.Inotrope for right ventricular support: Dobutamine or milrinone. Consider inhaled nitric oxide or a pulmonary vasodilator if available
doseMap.Cautious fluid only: A failing dilated right ventricle is made worse by volume loading. This is the opposite of the reflex for an obstetric collapse with bleeding, and it is why the echo matters

doseMap.Cryoprecipitate or fibrinogen concentrat: Target fibrinogen above 2 g/L. In amniotic fluid embolism the coagulopathy is often more immediately lethal than the cardiac event, and it will not respond to red cells alone
doseMap.Calcium replacement: 10 mL of 10% calcium chloride, repeated, guided by ionised calcium

data.label: Cardiac arrest and perimortem delivery
data.narrative: She arrests in pulseless electrical activity at minute 6. Perimortem caesarean is started at 4 minutes into the arrest and the infant is delivered at 4 minutes 40 seconds, Apgar 3 then 7 after resuscitation. Maternal circulation returns 90 seconds after delivery, which is the effect the procedure is designed to produce.

data.label: Assign someone to the husband, and debrief the team afterwards (Empathy)
data.narrative: Her husband watched his wife's abdomen opened on a delivery bed. You assign a senior midwife to stay with him from that moment, rather than leaving him in a corridor for two hours as usually happens. Afterwards, you insist on a team debrief at 08:00 rather than letting everyone go home: the junior midwife who was holding the fetal monitor is 23 and has just watched a perimortem caesarean, and she is going to remember whether anyone spoke to her. Pi Pim runs the debrief and says the department loses more staff to unprocessed nights like this one than to salaries.

data.label: Post-arrest ICU care and haemorrhage control
actions: ICU admission with targeted temperature management
Uterine haemostasis: balloon tamponade or B-Lynch suture

doseMap.Uterine haemostasis: balloon tamponade o: Hysterectomy if bleeding is uncontrolled, but only after fibrinogen has been corrected. Operating into an uncorrected coagulopathy makes the bleeding worse

data.label: Survival with organ support
data.narrative: Total transfusion: 14 units of red cells, 12 of plasma, 20 of cryoprecipitate, 3 pools of platelets. Uterus preserved with a balloon. Extubated day 4. Mild cognitive impairment from the hypoxic period, improving at three months. Reported survival has improved substantially with early recognition and aggressive product replacement.

data.label: Disposition
data.narrative: Discharged day 16 with her daughter. Referred to the national amniotic fluid embolism registry. She is counselled that recurrence in a future pregnancy has been reported but is not clearly increased, which is an honest answer rather than a reassuring one. The unit reviews its perimortem caesarean readiness and moves the scalpel pack into every delivery room.
